newsitem.title: USA: U.S. proposes waiver of int'l air liability limits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. proposes waiver of int'l air liability limits.

text.p: The U.S. Transportation Department said it tentatively approved a carrier agreement waiving a liability limit for passengers and their families in the event of death or injury on international flights.

The proposed changes would break a 25-year stalemate on the issue, the department said. Currently, liability is limited to $75,000 unless it can be proved a carrier was guilty of "willful misconduct," an extreme form of gross negligence.
Final approval, which would waive the Warsaw Convention's liability limit, is expected by the end of the year.

"These agreements, when put into force, will create a system based on a more fair standard of carrier liability for the deaths and injuries of passengers," Transportation Secretary Federico Pena said in a statement.
Interested parties have until October 24 to register opposition to the tentative decision and must show cause as to why it should not be made final, the department said.
